River Indie User Manual | Getting Started What is an Electric Scooter? An electric scooter such as the Indie is driven by a motor which is powered by a rechargeable battery, while traditional vehicles are powered by an internal combustion engine which runs by burning fossil fuels. Consequently, electric scooters are eco-friendly as they do not require fuel and do not emit exhaust gases. Characteristics of Indie 1. Indie runs on energy stored in the lithium-ion battery pack which powers the motor. It is more efficient in traffic since the motor does not idle like an engine and has fewer moving parts. The battery pack also powers auxiliary units such as the lamps, instrument cluster and other connected peripherals. 2. Indie is charged using a provided charger which can be plugged into a residential 16A power socket. This allows you to charge at home without having to refuel at a petrol station. You can charge it like any other portable electronic device such as a mobile phone. 3. Indie is equipped with regenerative braking. This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

Indie is charged using a provided charger which can be plugged into a residential 16A power socket. This allows you to charge at home without having to refuel at a petrol station. You can charge it like any other portable electronic device such as a mobile phone. 3. Indie is equipped with regenerative braking. This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

River Indie User Manual | Getting Started What is an Electric Scooter? An electric scooter such as the Indie is driven by a motor which is powered by a rechargeable battery, while traditional vehicles are powered by an internal combustion engine which runs by burning fossil fuels. Consequently, electric scooters are eco-friendly as they do not require fuel and do not emit exhaust gases. Characteristics of Indie 1. Indie runs on energy stored in the lithium-ion battery pack which powers the motor. It is more efficient in traffic since the motor does not idle like an engine and has fewer moving parts. The battery pack also powers auxiliary units such as the lamps, instrument cluster and other connected peripherals. 2. Indie is charged using a provided charger which can be plugged into a residential 16A power socket. This allows you to charge at home without having to refuel at a petrol station. You can charge it like any other portable electronic device such as a mobile phone. 3. Indie is equipped with regenerative braking. This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

RIGIDITY TEST - Determines the rigidity of the shell of the helmet by measuring the deformation of the helmet shell when progressively more load is applied up to a set limit. 4.16. Traction Control Traction Control limits wheel slip during aggressive riding and low grip conditions. TC has 4 modes - RAIN, ROAD, TRACK and RALLY. • Rain mode is suitable for low traction surfaces. • Road mode is designed for everyday use. • Track mode maintains optimal traction for aggressive riding conditions. • Rally mode provides optimized traction over loose surfaces. 4.17. Super Hold Super Hold prevents rolling of the vehicle on inclined surfaces without the rider having to apply brakes continuously. Both forward and reverse rolling are controlled by Super Hold. To activate, bring the vehicle to a standstill on the inclined surface by applying brakes. Once the brakes are left, the vehicle will continue to be at a standstill. CORRECT USE OF HEADLAMP High Beam Dazzling Oncoming Vehicle High Beam Dazzling Vehicle In Front NOTE Improper use of high beam can dazzle others and cause safety risks. Riding in high beam in specific condition can be punishable as per Motor Vehicle Act. Use Low beam when: • Riding in the city, on lit roads, or when other vehicles are around. • Riding closely behind someone, to prevent dazzling them through their mirrors. • Riding in bad weather (rain/fog/snow). Low beam allows you to see the road better. Use High beam ONLY when: • Riding on dark, unlit roads outside city limits. • Riding on empty roads with no other vehicles around you. Use Pass switch when: • Overtaking someone. Flash it once or twice to signal your intent to overtake. • Driving around a blind corner or intersection to signal your presence. Dealing with glare: If an oncoming vehicle or someone behind you is blinding you: • Do not stare directly into the bright lights. Shift your gaze slightly while still staying attentive. • Reduce your speed and keep a safe distance from others. • Keep your helmet visor and spectacles (if using) clean and free from scratches. 10

Indie runs on energy stored in the lithium-ion battery pack which powers the motor. It is more efficient in traffic since the motor does not idle like an engine and has fewer moving parts. The battery pack also powers auxiliary units such as the lamps, instrument cluster and other connected peripherals. 2. Indie is charged using a provided charger which can be plugged into a residential 16A power socket. This allows you to charge at home without having to refuel at a petrol station. You can charge it like any other portable electronic device such as a mobile phone. 3. Indie is equipped with regenerative braking. This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

River Indie User Manual | Getting Started What is an Electric Scooter? An electric scooter such as the Indie is driven by a motor which is powered by a rechargeable battery, while traditional vehicles are powered by an internal combustion engine which runs by burning fossil fuels. Consequently, electric scooters are eco-friendly as they do not require fuel and do not emit exhaust gases. Characteristics of Indie 1. Indie runs on energy stored in the lithium-ion battery pack which powers the motor. It is more efficient in traffic since the motor does not idle like an engine and has fewer moving parts. The battery pack also powers auxiliary units such as the lamps, instrument cluster and other connected peripherals. 2. Indie is charged using a provided charger which can be plugged into a residential 16A power socket. This allows you to charge at home without having to refuel at a petrol station. You can charge it like any other portable electronic device such as a mobile phone. 3. Indie is equipped with regenerative braking. This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

Which tests do the Ather helmets go through?

IMPACT ABSORPTION TEST - Determines the impact energy that a helmet can absorb when dropped from a certain height. RIGIDITY TEST - Determines the rigidity of the shell of the helmet by measuring the deformation of the helmet shell when progressively more load is applied up to a set limit. RETENTION TEST - Determines the dynamic displacement, residual displacement and damage to the retention system in order to assess the suitability of the helmet.

Which tests do the Ather helmets go through?

IMPACT ABSORPTION TEST - Determines the impact energy that a helmet can absorb when dropped from a certain height. RIGIDITY TEST - Determines the rigidity of the shell of the helmet by measuring the deformation of the helmet shell when progressively more load is applied up to a set limit. RETENTION TEST - Determines the dynamic displacement, residual displacement and damage to the retention system in order to assess the suitability of the helmet.

Which tests do the Ather helmets go through?

IMPACT ABSORPTION TEST - Determines the impact energy that a helmet can absorb when dropped from a certain height. RIGIDITY TEST - Determines the rigidity of the shell of the helmet by measuring the deformation of the helmet shell when progressively more load is applied up to a set limit. RETENTION TEST - Determines the dynamic displacement, residual displacement and damage to the retention system in order to assess the suitability of the helmet.

When a rider applies excessive brake force while riding whether on a dry, wet, or loose surfaces like gravel, the wheels may stop spinning and lose traction. This loss of grip leads to instability, making the scooter prone to skidding and crashing. When a wheel locks and slips, it can cause a loss of control almost instantly. Regaining control under such conditions is often a matter of luck or requires advanced skill, like that of professional stunt riders. ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) prevents wheel lock by continuously monitoring wheel speed and modulating brake pressure. ANTI-LOCK BRAKE SYSTEM (ABS) Your TVS X is fitted with an Anti-lock braking system (ABS) is designed to prevent skidding & help riders to maintain steering control during emergency-stopping situation if dry or wet roads, loose gravels etc. How does ABS work? When a rider applies excessive brake force while riding whether on a dry, wet, or loose surfaces like gravel, the wheels may stop spinning and lose traction. This loss of grip leads to instability, making the scooter prone to skidding and crashing. When a wheel locks and slips, it can cause a loss of control almost instantly. Regaining control under such conditions is often a matter of luck or requires advanced skill, like that of professional stunt riders. ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) prevents wheel lock by continuously monitoring wheel speed and modulating brake pressure. When the system detects that a wheel is about to lock up, it reduces brake pressure momentarily to keep the wheel rotating. Once the risk of

When a rider applies excessive brake force while riding whether on a dry, wet, or loose surfaces like gravel, the wheels may stop spinning and lose traction. This loss of grip leads to instability, making the scooter prone to skidding and crashing. When a wheel locks and slips, it can cause a loss of control almost instantly. Regaining control under such conditions is often a matter of luck or requires advanced skill, like that of professional stunt riders. ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) prevents wheel lock by continuously monitoring wheel speed and modulating brake pressure. When the system detects that a wheel is about to lock up, it reduces brake pressure momentarily to keep the wheel rotating. Once the risk of

When a rider applies excessive brake force while riding whether on a dry, wet, or loose surfaces like gravel, the wheels may stop spinning and lose traction. This loss of grip leads to instability, making the scooter prone to skidding and crashing. When a wheel locks and slips, it can cause a loss of control almost instantly. Regaining control under such conditions is often a matter of luck or requires advanced skill, like that of professional stunt riders. ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) prevents wheel lock by continuously monitoring wheel speed and modulating brake pressure. River Indie User Manual | Getting Started What is an Electric Scooter? An electric scooter such as the Indie is driven by a motor which is powered by a rechargeable battery, while traditional vehicles are powered by an internal combustion engine which runs by burning fossil fuels. Consequently, electric scooters are eco-friendly as they do not require fuel and do not emit exhaust gases. Characteristics of Indie 1. Indie runs on energy stored in the lithium-ion battery pack which powers the motor. It is more efficient in traffic since the motor does not idle like an engine and has fewer moving parts. The battery pack also powers auxiliary units such as the lamps, instrument cluster and other connected peripherals. 2. Indie is charged using a provided charger which can be plugged into a residential 16A power socket. This allows you to charge at home without having to refuel at a petrol station. You can charge it like any other portable electronic device such as a mobile phone. 3. Indie is equipped with regenerative braking. This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

This aids in partially recharging the batteries while decelerating or riding downhill. This minimizes energy loss and increases efficiency and range. 9 9

ANTI-LOCK BRAKE SYSTEM (ABS) Your TVS X is fitted with an Anti-lock braking system (ABS) is designed to prevent skidding & help riders to maintain steering control during emergency-stopping situation if dry or wet roads, loose gravels etc. How does ABS work? When a rider applies excessive brake force while riding whether on a dry, wet, or loose surfaces like gravel, the wheels may stop spinning and lose traction. This loss of grip leads to instability, making the scooter prone to skidding and crashing. When a wheel locks and slips, it can cause a loss of control almost instantly. Regaining control under such conditions is often a matter of luck or requires advanced skill, like that of professional stunt riders. ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) prevents wheel lock by continuously monitoring wheel speed and modulating brake pressure. When the system detects that a wheel is about to lock up, it reduces brake pressure momentarily to keep the wheel rotating. Once the risk of

9.2. Charging My Battery 9.2.1. Charging your scooter The Charger can be used to recharge the vehicle’s battery conveniently and safely. When the Charger connector is connected to the vehicle inlet, a communication link is established between the Charger and the vehicle. The charge cycle is initiated automatically and is dependent on the demand of the vehicle. The vehicle controls the charging rate during the charge cycle, and the Charger will stop supplying power to the vehicle when the battery is fully charged, as indicated by the vehicle. If necessary, you can stop the charge cycle by disconnecting the power supply to the Charger. If the Charger remains connected to the vehicle, you can resume an interrupted charge cycle by switching the power supply back ON.
